text:
salesops-bot: Heads up — StitchPay reported large latency regressions starting ~08:15 UTC after yesterday's routing deploy. They see 3x p50 for short chat flows and user friction across multiple regions. Asking for a prioritization decision and whether we can route them to a safer model variant while we investigate. Customer is on a paid Dedicated plan. :warning:

Maya K: Thanks — putting details here. Logs from their session attached in support ticket. Short summary: high tail when requests hit region eu-west-1, mostly sequences < 120 tokens. They repro with this curl:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hello"}'
```

Jordan P: @Maya K do we know if KV cache warmup difference could explain it? The deploy swapped the routing policy to prefer low-cost variants which might be cold.

Maya K: Not confirmed. Support saw increased cold starts and a spike in model swap events in the logs. Example trace snippet:```
[2028-05-02T08:16:12Z] route-switch model=rwd-3b->rwd-3b-q8 reason=cost-fallthrough
[2028-05-02T08:16:12Z] kvcache-miss session=stitch-usr-234
```

Liam R: Can we do a short mitigation: add a policy to pin StitchPay requests to the stable variant (rwd-3b-stable) for the next 48h and monitor? That avoids infra churn while we root-cause.

Aro (prod): That sounds reasonable. We should confirm cost impact with sales first — their contract allows limited burst. Also we need an engineer owner to implement routing override and validate no cascade effects.

Maya K: I can loop in the AE for cost signoff. Who can own the routing override? Estimated effort: 1-2hrs to add a tenant-level routing exception + smoke test.

Jordan P: @Liam R can you own the override? If this is quick we can ship the change and then do deeper profiling next sprint.

Liam R: I can take it. Plan: add tenant-route override -> force rwd-3b-stable -> run 30m Canary traffic and compare p50/p95. If good, keep for 48h. I'll also capture kernel selection and batch size histograms.

Maya K: Thanks — I'll escalate to sales and confirm approval. Please also add a short note for product: this is a potential small-but-repeatable customer ask to support tenant pins for routing; might be worth adding to backlog as a configurable emergency button.

Jordan P: Agreed. Product question: is this an ops-only band-aid or a product feature? If we make it a product feature, scope includes UI, ACLs, audit logs, and rollout safety checks. That would be a 2-sprint project with QA.

Liam R: For now ops-only. We'll implement a controlled override and create a ticket to scope product work.

Maya K: Created backlog item PROD-6779 to track feature-scoping (will paste link once created). Also created incident ticket INC-9123 for current customer case.

deploy-bot: deploy started by Liam R at 08:45 UTC: route-override/stitchpay -> rwd-3b-stable :rocket:

Liam R: Override is live. Running canary now (10% of traffic). Early numbers: p50 down ~25%, p95 down ~18% on canary. Will expand to 50% in 30m if stable.

Aro (prod): Please snapshot traces and attach to INC-9123. Also make sure to capture cost delta.

Maya K: AE confirmed short-term cost ok. Sales asks we keep them informed hourly. Will post updates to the customer channel. :thumbsup:

Jordan P: Next steps for product: add scoped spec doc for tenant routing pins; include acceptance criteria: audit trail, max-duration TTL, ACL by account role, revert automation. Assign to product backlog grooming.

Liam R: I'll add logs and the kernel/batching histograms to the incident. If the root cause is model variant cold-starts, longer-term fix could be pre-warm heuristics or smarter prefix caching.

Maya K: Thanks team. Summary: routing override applied and improved latencies; sales notified; product to scope feature (PROD-6779); engineering owns immediate follow-up (Liam) and will report back in 6 hours with full metrics. :eyes:
